subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: I know when to use who, where, that/which and when.
I can join information with relative pronouns.
I can write definitions like “It’s a place where …”.

tf.why: He’s the doctor who Julia saw.
We use where for places; that/which is for things.
I remember the time when you went to hospital.

tf.s: “Camels are animals who live in the desert.” is the best answer in the lesson.
tf.why: For animals and things we use that: animals that live in the desert.

tf.s: “A pharmacy is a shop where you can buy medicine.” is correct.
tf.why: A shop is a place, so we use where.

tf.s: We can use that or which for things.
tf.why: What’s the book that you want to read?

tf.s: “A chef is a person where cooks in a restaurant.” is correct.
tf.why: A chef is a person, so we use who.

tf.s: In the listening, the film is called Summer Nights.
tf.why: The film is called Summer Days.

tf.s: The new cinema is next to the office building where Dad works.
tf.why: Yes, it is next to Dad’s office building.

tf.s: “Winter is the time where the weather gets colder.” is correct.
tf.why: For time we use when: the time when …

boxes.q: Which pronoun do we use for people?
Which pronoun do we use for places?
Which pronoun do we use for time?
Complete: A mechanic is someone ___ can fix machines.
boxes.why: A mechanic is a person: who.

boxes.q: Complete: Eid is a time ___ people give presents.
boxes.why: Eid is a time, so we use when.

boxes.q: Complete: A smartphone is a device ___ you use to send messages.
boxes.why: A device is a thing: that/which.

boxes.q: Complete: The hospital is the place ___ Julia went.

boxes.why: The film is called Summer Days.

boxes.q: Complete: It’s a place ___ you go when you are very sick.
Complete: Camels are animals ___ live in the desert.
boxes.why: For animals we use that or which.

hunt.q: A chef is a person ___ cooks.
A library is a place ___ you read.
Winter is the time ___ it’s cold.
A pen is a thing ___ you write with.
A place where you go when very sick

o: that/which – things; where – places; when – time; who – people
who – things; where – time; when – people
mcq.why: This is the grammar table from the lesson.

o: next to the office building where Dad works
mcq.why: It is next to Dad’s office building.

o: He’s the doctor who Julia saw.
It’s the place who we live.
It’s the day who we met.
It’s the book who I read.
mcq.why: A doctor is a person, so who is correct.

o: A stadium is a place where you can watch matches.
A teacher is a person where helps us.
Friday is a day where we rest.
A pen is a thing where you write.
It’s a place where you can read and borrow books.
It’s a person who reads books.
It’s a time when you read books.
It’s a place who you read books.
mcq.why: A library is a place: It’s a place where …

o: She’s a person who brings food in a café.
It’s a place where you eat.
It’s a time when you eat.
It’s a thing which you eat.
mcq.why: A waitress is a person, so we use who.

mcq.q: Join: “I remember the day. We visited the chocolate factory that day.”
o: I remember the day when we visited the chocolate factory.
I remember the day who we visited the chocolate factory.
I remember the day where we visited the chocolate factory.
I remember the day what we visited the chocolate factory.
A bus is a thing who takes people to school.
A bus is a thing that takes people to school.
A café is a place where you can drink tea.
A nurse is a person who helps doctors.
mcq.why: A bus is a thing, so we use that or which, not who.

mcq.q: “It’s a person who …” – what kind of word is the answer?
o: a job or a person, like a chef
mcq.why: who always tells us about a person.

mcq.q: Why do we use where in “the apartment building where Sharifa lives”?
o: Because the apartment building is a place.
mcq.why: where gives information about a place.
